key_insight: OmniStream unifies perception, reconstruction and action in a single streaming visual backbone by applying causal spatiotemporal and geometry-aware processing, enabling real-time, physically grounded understanding from continuous visual inputs.
problem_solved: Bridges fragmented visual foundations (static image perception, offline temporal models, and separate geometry modules) to deliver a single model that operates causally and continuously for real-time embodied tasks.
method: Causal spatiotemporal attention: process incoming frames in a streaming, low-latency manner that preserves temporal causality for online decision-making.
Unified representation: fuse semantic perception, implicit/explicit 3D reconstruction, and action-ready features in one backbone with task-specific heads.
Efficiency and memory design: streaming buffer and sparse attention/compute mechanisms to keep inference real-time while supporting long-range temporal context.
impact: Simplifies pipelines for embodied agents and robotics by providing a single, real-time backbone that generalizes across perception, 3D reconstruction and control — improving responsiveness and deployment practicality.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: streaming camera input → causal spatiotemporal backbone → branched heads (perception, reconstruction, action).
Timeline visualization: causal attention window vs. full-context offline models (latency and information flow highlighted).
Before/after examples: monocular frames and the corresponding reconstructed 3D scene + agent action overlaid.
Performance chart: accuracy/quality vs. latency tradeoff and ablation bars showing contribution of causal attention and geometry modules.
paper_title: OmniStream: Mastering Perception, Reconstruction and Action in Continuous Streams
paper_authors: Yibin Yan, Jilan Xu, Shangzhe Di, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie
